title: Bevacizumab + weekly paclitaxel

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps blood vessels grow. Blocking it can restrict the blood supply supporting a tumour. It also affects normal blood vessels and healing, which is why blood pressure, urine and planned procedures matter.
agents.watch: Report bleeding, a wound that is not healing, severe abdominal pain, new swelling, chest symptoms or a severe headache. Tell the team before surgery, dental procedures or port insertion.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
agents.watch: Report tingling or numbness before the next weekly dose, especially if it affects walking or hand use. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest or throat tightness, itching, dizziness or breathing changes during infusion.
risks: Hair loss, muscle or joint pain
Mouth, bowel, skin and nail effects

context_label: First-line metastatic breast cancer · source-defined eligibility
purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
schedule_summary: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg is given on Days 1 and 15, with paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Continue according to benefit, toxicity and the treating team’s plan.

urgent_extra: Seek urgent advice for major bleeding, severe headache or visual change, chest pain, breathlessness, one-sided weakness, severe abdominal pain, fever or poor wound healing.

support.title: Blood pressure and urine
support.text: Attend the required checks even if you feel well. Report severe headache, visual change or swelling.

support.title: Operations and dental work
support.text: Tell oncology about planned procedures; bevacizumab timing and wound healing need review.

support.title: Paclitaxel premedicines
support.text: The first dose and later doses have different plans. A previous reaction changes the assessment.

support.title: Nerves and bleeding
support.text: Report numbness, unusual bleeding or bruising before the next visit.

questions.q: Why was this treatment chosen for me?
questions.a: Bevacizumab blocks VEGF-driven blood-vessel signalling while paclitaxel disrupts cell division. Treatment selection considers the first-line setting, cancer biology, alternatives and the balance between disease control and vascular, bleeding and nerve risks.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed or missed?
questions.a: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

questions.q: Who arranges the checks and explains the results?
questions.a: Agree the due window, booking team, result reviewer and contact route if a test or appointment is missing. This page does not record completed checks.

questions.q: Can I take other medicines or supplements?
questions.a: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg is given on Days 1 and 15, with paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Continue according to benefit, toxicity and the treating team’s plan.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver tests and urine protein. Review blood counts, renal/liver function and urine protein before cycles; Day 8 FBC is explicitly required. Check current counts for each paclitaxel decision.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Measure blood pressure before each bevacizumab dose and follow the agreed urine-protein plan. Review bleeding, clotting, wounds and planned procedures. Cardiac imaging is considered for prior anthracycline/chest radiotherapy or clinical concern; warfarin requires additional INR monitoring.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: Agree the scan type and review interval for the known disease sites. Review response, symptoms and toxicity together; new or worsening symptoms may need an earlier assessment.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Review response, toxicity and priorities to decide whether to continue, change or stop. Supportive and palliative care can accompany anticancer treatment.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.

steps.title: Before treatment
steps.text: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver tests and urine protein. Review blood counts, renal/liver function and urine protein before cycles; Day 8 FBC is explicitly required. Check current counts for each paclitaxel decision.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. A port is not automatically required; insertion and removal are separate procedures with individual instructions.

steps.title: On the treatment day
steps.text: Confirm the medicines due that day, any premedicines and the reviewed blood results. Tell staff immediately about pain, burning, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: No routine take-home infusion pump is required for this regimen. Keep line-care, urgent-contact and next-review instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: Bevacizumab: 90 minutes initially, then 60 and 30 minutes if tolerated; paclitaxel: about one hour. Full visit time is longer.

details.title: Line care
details.text: A PICC or port has its own care plan. Report fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or line damage; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: Treatment changes
details.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

details.title: Support for this visit
details.text: Separate the first paclitaxel premedication from later weekly doses; review blood pressure, urine protein, wounds and surgery timing for bevacizumab.

anatomy: Severe headache or visual change needs urgent review.
Protein checks can detect problems before symptoms; report swelling.
Severe abdominal pain or poor wound healing needs urgent advice.
Report bleeding; sudden chest, breathing or stroke symptoms are emergencies.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology.
Report tingling or numbness before the next dose.
